Coinbase is building the future of finance for people, institutions and their agents, with one place to trade crypto, equities, derivatives and prediction markets, use stablecoins, and connect AI agents with clear controls. • Partner directly with enterprise customers and internal product teams to convert roadmap into live customers.

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As a Program Manager on Anthropic's Safeguards team, you'll help make sure we meet our obligations under AI safety laws and regulations around the world. Working closely with Legal, you'll turn new and emerging requirements into programs, controls, and deliverables. This requires a detailed understanding of how our models and products are built, evaluated and safeguarded. Your work will support Anthropic's commitment to developing AI safely and beneficially as the regulatory landscape evolves.

The responsibilities listed below are some examples of areas that someone in this role could own, depending on their experience and the team's needs.

Key responsibilities

•
Manage and drive complex safety initiatives that identify, assess and mitigate risks from frontier models, from initial risk assessment through to the deployment of safeguards

•
Partner with the Safeguards incident management team to strengthen incident response and reporting processes, including the policies that determine how incidents are escalated and when they must be reported externally

•
Conduct post-incident reviews, and work with the subject matter experts for each harm area to incorporate the findings into model and product safeguards

•
Own the safety strategy and deliverables for AI systems used in high-risk settings, including risk assessments, technical documentation, and the information that deploying customers need to use those systems safely

•
Define the safety and risk controls that our models and products require, ensure that each control has an owner and a documented procedure, and confirm that it operates as intended

•
Partner closely with the owners of each risk area to develop a deep understanding of AI risks, safety evaluations and mitigation strategies, and use that understanding to prepare safety documentation, transparency reports and regulatory submissions

Minimum qualifications

•
Experience in trust and safety, AI safety or a related field, including designing and implementing safeguards against misuse or harm

•
Understanding of AI safety, including the principal risk areas and the evaluations and safeguards used to address them, well enough to engage substantively with the technical experts responsible for them

•
Experience running risk assessment or harm mitigation programs from identification through to resolution

•
Experience translating policy or regulatory requirements into practical operational processes

•
Ability to drive complex, cross-functional programs to completion in a fast-moving environment, including with technical teams outside your own discipline

•
Clear written communication, including documentation for technical, legal and external audiences

•
Strong attention to detail, and the judgment to recognize when work is at risk and raise it early

•
Commitment to the safe development and deployment of AI

Preferred qualifications

•
Experience with AI-specific regulation, such as the EU AI Act

•
Experience leading incident response programs, including escalation paths and external reporting obligations

•
Experience preparing safety documentation, transparency reports or regulatory submissions

•
Experience working with technical and research teams on safety evaluations

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$245,000 — $285,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.description:
Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) accelerates digital transformation so customers can be more agile, efficient, resilient, and secure. The Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange platform protects thousands of customers from cyberattacks and data loss by securely connecting users, devices, and applications in any location. Distributed across 200+ public data centers globally and thousands of private sites at the edge, the SASE-based Zero Trust Exchange is the world’s largest in-line cloud security platform.

We believe the future of work is Human + AI and are building an AI-native enterprise where human potential is amplified by machine intelligence to solve the world’s hardest security challenges. Driven by deep customer obsession, we are committed to the mission, outcome, and to each other. We bring these commitments to life through three core behaviors: ownership and collaboration, trust through outcomes and impact, and a challenge culture with ongoing feedback. Ready to make an impact at the company pioneering security transformation in the AI era? Join us at Zscaler.

Role

We are looking for a Principal Software Development Engineer to join our team. This hands-on role in Santa Clara,CA, reporting to the Director of Engineering in the Digital Experience department. As the Principal Software Development Engineer for ZDX UI, you will be the visionary architect leading the charge into the next era of enterprise observability: AI-first user experiences. You won't just build dashboards; you will reinvent how enterprise IT, network and security teams troubleshoot and remediate user experience issues at global scale. You will champion an AI-augmented engineering culture—utilizing agents and automate engineering pipelines to accelerate development velocity.

What you’ll do (Role Expectations)

• Visualize next-gen diagnostic intelligence by creating highly performant, real-time data visualizations (using D3, WebGL, or Canvas) to turn complex network telemetry into intuitive, natural-language root-cause narratives

• Turn complex data into clear customer action by partnering with Product, UX, backend, and platform teams to deliver intuitive dashboards and prototyping AI-assisted experiences where they demonstrably improve customer outcomes

• Own frontend performance, accessibility, security, automated testing, observability, and production readiness while enforcing code reviews, independent validation, and safeguards for sensitive data

• Lead hands-on with AI coding assistants and agentic development tools across discovery, implementation, and debugging, turning successful experiments into repeatable team practices

• Raise the team’s engineering capability by mentoring engineers and setting frontend technical direction by architecting scalable React components and shared UI foundations for ZDX and Experience Center integration

Who You Are (Success Profile)

• You are customer-obsessed, anchoring UI decisions in real troubleshooting needs and judging success by how effortlessly customers can understand complex problems and take action.

• You are driven by innovation, actively exploring AI tools and new engineering approaches, conducting practical experiments, and scaling what works while distinguishing genuine improvement from mere novelty.

• You act like an owner, taking full responsibility from initial technical direction through to production outcomes, maintaining absolute accountability for code correctness, security, and maintainability.

• You champion simplicity, effortlessly distilling complex data, requirements, and system architectures into intuitive user experiences and clear engineering plans.

• You are a high-trust collaborator, building alignment across teams, communicating technical tradeoffs candidly, and helping others grow by sharing AI workflows, lessons learned, and constructive feedback.

What We’re Looking for (Minimum Qualifications)

• Demonstrated curiosity and active exploration of AI tools, with a proven history of integrating new technologies to enhance daily workflows and augment problem-solving. Hands-on use of AI coding assistants or agentic development tools in real engineering work, with concrete examples of improved delivery or quality and the ability to explain how outputs were validated

• Demonstrated experience architecting and delivering complex, production-grade enterprise web applications, with technical leadership across multiple engineers or teams

• Deep expertise in JavaScript, React, HTML, CSS, and browser fundamentals, including component design, asynchronous programming, and state management such as Redux or equivalent approaches

• Experience building data-intensive interfaces and integrating APIs, with sound approaches to client-side caching, filtering, pagination, error handling, and rendering performance

• Proven ability to deliver reliable frontend software through automated unit, integration, and end-to-end testing; performance profiling; accessible and secure UI design; and production debugging

• Ability to translate ambiguous requirements into clear technical designs, communicate architectural tradeoffs, mentor engineers, and lead cross-functional delivery without relying on reporting authority, including helping peers adopt effective and responsible AI-assisted development practices

What Will Make You Stand Out (Preferred Qualifications)

• Proven ability to leverage AI technologies and workflows to drive measurable operational efficiency

• Experience with digital experience monitoring, observability, network or application performance products, or interactive visualization of time-series and high-volume telemetry

• Experience evolving shared frontend platforms, design systems, or micro-frontends across product teams, including TypeScript adoption, package versioning, CI/CD, and backward-compatible migrations

• Experience scaling AI-assisted engineering beyond personal use through reusable agent workflows, repository guidance, automated validation, or team enablement, with measured results; experience building grounded, transparent AI-assisted analytics or troubleshooting interfaces is an additional advantage

Who are we?
Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.
We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.
We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.
We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!
Role Overview:
We're growing our Canadian Public Sector Delivery team and hiring Public Sector Delivery Analysts to help run some of the most consequential AI deployments in the country. You'll work alongside our Engineering Program Managers (EPMs), Technical Leads, and senior leadership to keep large, multi-stakeholder government programs organized, documented, and moving.
This is a hands-on delivery role for individuals who want exposure to enterprise AI and high-stakes program delivery while taking pride in making complex programs run smoothly. As a member of our small, senior team, you'll deliver sovereign AI to the Government of Canada, engage directly with clients from day one on a clear path toward leading engagements, and learn how frontier AI products are deployed in real, high-security environments.

Key Responsibilities:
• Drive things to closure. Partner with the EPM and Technical Leads to track actions, dependencies, and blockers across Cohere and client teams making sure nothing slips.

• Show up in front of the client. Prepare and coordinate client sessions, capture outcomes, and progressively lead working-level sessions such as use-case and story refinement.

• Run the cadence. Own the meeting and reporting rhythm including agendas, scheduling, minutes, and follow-ups so every forum lands on time with clear next steps.

• Own the delivery artefacts. Build and maintain the plans, status reports, RAID logs, decision records, use-case registers, and traceability documentation that keep our engagements audit-ready and our clients confident.

• Keep the record straight. Maintain a single source of truth for program documentation in our public sector document management environment.

Qualifications:
• 1–4 years of experience in technology or management consulting, professional services, or an in-house technical delivery team.

• Delivery discipline. You've run RAID, action, and decision logs, refined user stories, maintained project plans on real projects and kept them accurate and clear.

• Client presence. You can lead a working session in front of a client, read the room, and know what to say and what to hold.

• Strong written communication. You think through the message before you build the slide. Advanced PowerPoint, Word, and Excel.

• Technical fluency. You're comfortable discussing APIs, integrations, environments, testing, and releases. You can talk with engineers and report back accurately.

• Follow-through. You close items without a second reminder and know what to escalate and when.

• Eligibility for a Government of Canada security clearance.

• Based in the Ottawa area.

• University Degree in Business/Commerce, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering or similar preferred.

• Nice-to-have: High degree of French language proficiency.

Working Location:
This role is hybrid with the requirement to be based out of Ottawa - note, there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement.
This role requires eligibility for a Government of Canada security clearance and a high degree of French language proficiency is a nice-to-have.

Full-Time Employees at Cohere enjoy these Perks:
• A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

• Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

• RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

• 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

• Annual enrichment benefits:
Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

• 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

• Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How and Where We Work:
• Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

• For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

• For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

• Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

jobs.description:
About the Team
The Frontier Assurance team brings independent scrutiny into OpenAI’s safety decisions and helps the public understand and assess our safety work. We lead third-party assessments and safeguard testing for OpenAI’s flagship launches, pilot new assurance mechanisms such as embedded auditing, run our misalignment disclosure process, and incorporate independent expert input as evidence for critical safety decisions.
About the Role
As a Research Program Manager on the Frontier Assurance team, you will build programs that bring independent expertise into frontier AI safety decisions and make the evidence behind those decisions understandable to the public. You will lead external research partnerships and third-party assessments, coordinate public safety documentation, and develop new approaches to independent scrutiny and transparency. Working across research, engineering, product, policy, and communications, you will help ensure external findings inform concrete decisions and that our public explanations accurately reflect the evidence, limitations, and remaining uncertainty.
We’re looking for people with deep experience in research partnerships and program management with technical and research teams. This role combines partnership management, cross-functional coordination, an understanding of AI safety research, alignment, and evaluations, and strong communication skills. You will work with researchers and engineers within OpenAI and across the external community to initiate projects, set ambitious goals and milestones, and drive execution across multiple teams.
This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.
In this role, you will:
• Design and run third-party assessment programs for frontier models and safeguards, including independent evaluations, adversarial testing, and new approaches such as embedded auditing. Work with researchers and external partners to define assessment questions, scope, access, timelines, and deliverables.

• Build and manage strategic research partnerships with third-party evaluators, academic labs, and other independent experts, prioritizing expertise, independence, and diversity of perspectives. Enable rigorous research, including work that challenges internal assumptions.

• Bring external findings to safety decision-makers and translate them into actionable recommendations for safeguards, deployment, product, and policy. Track follow-up actions and ensure partners understand how their input was considered.

You might thrive in this role if you:
• Have an understanding of AI evaluations and measurement, and can engage with technical teams on evaluation design and results.

• Have experience building research partnerships and managing external stakeholders, especially academic researchers and independent experts.

• Can synthesize technical and social science research into clear executive summaries and accessible explanations for public audiences.

• Have experience delivering technical publications or public reports across multiple contributors, and exercising judgment about what to share, with whom, and when.
